rationale: Round 0 built and passed, so this round pushes obfuscation harder: IGV gets the highest weights because Blowfish's identity is dominated by large static constant tables (P-array and four S-boxes in bf_pi.h, ~325 lines) that are ideal for constant/global obfuscation with near-zero steady-state runtime cost once initialized; SUB is next since Blowfish's XOR/add/OR round function is highly substitutable and diversifies the hot crypto core cheaply; FLA and BCF are kept moderately high to obscure the 16-round Feistel loop and the large non-critical test/print_test_data functions (which dominate text size, so their SizeCost weights are raised to steer flattening/bogus-flow toward code where the size tax is acceptable); SPLIT stays low-cost/safe and applies broadly as a cheap diversity base; IBR and ICALL are moderate because Blowfish has few calls and indirect branching in the hot BF_encrypt loop carries real runtime cost, so their RuntimeCost weights (0.6/0.45) temper application in performance-sensitive functions while still allowing use in setup paths like BF_set_key. CorrectnessRisk weights stay low across the board given round 0's clean pass, but FLA's is highest to keep flattening off fragile loop-carried structures.
